chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aslam narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I said to him: “May I be your ransom, a man killed another man, intentionally or by mistake, and he had a debt and property. Then his heirs wanted to remit his blood to the killer.” So he said: “If they remit his blood, they become responsible for the debt.”
I said: “What if they want to execute him?” He said: “If he was killed intentionally, his killer is executed, and the Imam pays the debt on his behalf from the share of the debtors.”

I said: “If he was killed intentionally and his heirs made a settlement with his killer for the diyyah, then upon whom is the debt: upon his heirs out of the diyyah, or upon the Imam of the Muslims?” He said: “Rather, they pay his debt from his diyyah which his heirs agreed upon in settlement, for he has more right to his diyyah than anyone else.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: His legal heirs or those entitled to act regarding his blood claim.
key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The Imam as the public authority responsible in certain legal-financial cases.
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: Blood money paid in settlement for homicide.
key_terms.دَمَهُ: His blood claim, meaning the right of retaliation or pardon in homicide.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A financial debt owed by the deceased victim.
key_terms.سَهْمِ الْغَارِمِينَ: The allocated share for debtors from public religious funds.

ai.seo_question: Who pays the debt of a murdered person if the heirs pardon the killer, seek qiṣāṣ, or accept diyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about debts owed by a slain person in cases of pardon, qiṣāṣ, and settlement on diyyah. It explains that if the heirs waive retaliation they assume the debt, if qiṣāṣ is carried out the Imam pays from the share of al-ghārimīn, and if the heirs accept diyyah the debt is paid from that diyyah first.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5220 - Muhammad ibn Aslam narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as): "May I be your ransom! A man was killed, whether intentionally or accidentally, and he had debts and wealth. His heirs wanted to pardon the killer. What is the ruling?" Imam (as) said: "If they pardon his blood, they are responsible for paying his debts."

I asked: "What if they wish to execute the killer?" Imam (as) said: "If he is killed intentionally, his killer is to be executed, and the Imam will pay his debt from the gharimin (debtors) portion of the public treasury (Bayt Al-Mal)."

I asked: "If he was killed intentionally and his heirs reconciled with the killer for blood money (diyyah), who is responsible for the debt? Is it upon his heirs from the blood money or upon the Imam of the Muslims?" Imam (as) replied: "Rather, they must pay his debt from the diyyah they accepted in the settlement because he is more entitled to his blood money than anyone else."
